about.title: How TasteAbroad works
about.intro: Rankings and price tell you where you could study. TasteAbroad answers the three questions that decide whether you will be happy there: will the culture of the city feel like home, can you study in a language you speak, and can you afford it?
about.stepsTitle: What happens when you press the button
about.step1: You type what you love: artists, films, shows, food, hobbies, brands or places.
about.step2: The TasteAbroad agent (built on Google Gemini) reads your list and calls tools. First it looks up every like on Qloo: a specific name becomes a Qloo entity (Dua Lipa, Studio Ghibli), a genre or hobby becomes a Qloo tag (techno, street food, hiking).
about.step3: Qloo then ranks all {count} university cities once for each of your tastes. Names go in directly; genres and hobbies go in through the artists and films Qloo links to them (jazz through Miles Davis and Diana Krall), because most tags have no city data of their own. A city's match score is its average position across your tastes.
about.step4: It asks Qloo what else people with the same taste like (music, films, TV, places).
about.step5: It reads our curated data for the best cities: well-known universities, typical international tuition, a monthly student budget and the languages you can study in.
about.step6: Finally the agent writes a short note for each city that refers to what you typed. In the compare view, Qloo also suggests places inside each city that people like you love.
about.roleQloo: Qloo decides where every city ranks for each of your tastes. The match score is calculated only from those rankings, and every card shows them. The agent never sets or changes a score.
about.roleAi: The agent decides which Qloo lookups to make and puts the results into words. It can only use cities and IDs that Qloo actually returned.
about.roleData: Universities, tuition and living costs come from our own dataset. They are rough ranges, so always check the official university site.
about.reliability: If the language model is busy or rate-limited, a backup pipeline calls the same Qloo tools in a fixed order, so you still get results. Identical searches are cached for 30 minutes and every visitor has a fair-use limit to protect the free API quotas.
about.limitsTitle: What the results do not mean
about.limits: Qloo describes what groups of people with similar tastes enjoy. A high score is not a prediction about you, and it says nothing about admission chances, visas or safety.
about.privacy: No account, no tracking. Only the things you type are sent to Qloo and Gemini to compute the result. Your search lives in the page link so you can share it.
